decisions.reason: As an adjacent wafer-level packaging extension with likely low carrying cost and continued relevance for complex semiconductor integration, it is worth keeping open despite still-uncertain demand.
This carrier wafer fits the firm's core thin-wafer handling capabilities and strategic direction very closely, so the option value remains high and the case for withdrawal is weak.
The copper interposer glass wafer is a strategically attractive but still uncertain advanced-packaging option, so management would keep it on the market to learn more before committing or abandoning.
An off-the-shelf brand is close to the established business and relatively inexpensive to maintain, making it a sensible commercial option to retain while testing broader market pull.

Glass-based circuit boards are the most distant from the firm's core offer and likely require disproportionate attention and development resources relative to the nearer, more credible options already in the portfolio.
